text:
sam: Hey folks — noticed a customer app saw duplicate side-effects after a burst of 429s yesterday. Not full blown duplicates but a few retries replayed the same POST after a token refresh.
anya: Ugh. Do we have an idempotency key in that flow?
sam: They thought so, but the client library only attaches idempotency for sync generate calls. This was a streaming/async webhook retry path.
neha: Are we sure it was 429-triggered or auth refresh race? Logs show refresh at 12:03:11 and two sends at 12:03:12-12:03:13.
quinn: Could be unsafe-replay window + no jitter on our side. The client retried immediately when it saw 429 and the refresh happened concurrently.
sam: Here's the snippet from their SDK logs: ```
# client retry
POST /v1/responses  429 -> retry()
start_token_refresh()
retry immediate
POST /v1/responses 200
```
anya: That pattern screams unsafe immediate retry. We recommend jittered exponential backoff for any 429 + token refresh. Might need a client-side guard to block replay while refresh in flight.
neha: Agreed. We already have replay-guard in Node SDK but streaming/async sampleapps miss it. Should we push a patch to sample app and docs?
quinn: Yes — two parts: (1) sampleapp update with a small locker around auth refresh + queued retries, and (2) a guidance note: "avoid immediate retried side-effects when auth rotation is pending".
sam: Also saw they send idempotency-key header but the backend treats these POSTs as non-idempotent for streaming responses. So key present != safe if server-side handler isn't checking. 
replay-bot: Incident 2025-03-11-dup-replays created for tracking. Tags: devex, sdk-parity, idempotency.
anya: For SDK parity: Node/Go have replay-guard but Python doesn't in streaming helper. Can we triage priority? Customer impact is low but dangerous for payment-like side-effects.
neha: I'll open a small RFC with recommended behavior: - attach idempotency header for all outbound side-effectful requests - if token refresh in flight, buffer new requests up to N ms - use randomized jittered backoff on 429 - expose a simple "safeReplay" toggle in SDKs
quinn: + add telemetry: emit a metric when a retry occurs during refresh and when idempotency-key mismatch occurs, so customers can debug.
sam: For the immediate fix: add a small debounce (150-300ms) on client retry after 429 when recently refresh-started. That avoids the most common race.
anya: Can we include a code snippet in sampleapp? Something like: ```js
// naive lock
let refreshing = false;
async function send(req) {
  if (refreshing) await wait(randomBetween(150, 300));
  try { return await fetch(req); }
  catch (e) { if (is429(e)) return retryWithBackoff(req); throw e }
}
async function refreshToken() { refreshing = true; await doRefresh(); refreshing = false }
```
neha: That will help. Also update docs to call out that idempotency keys require server-side enforcement. Add a small checklist for customers: 1) confirm idempotency handler 2) enable client retry jitter 3) enable SDK replay-guard 4) surface retry telemetry
quinn: Who wants to own sampleapp change? I can PR for Node and Go. Neha can do Python docs + sample.
sam: I'll reach out to the customer with mitigation steps and link the PRs when ready. Thanks all :thumbsup:
replay-bot: Added PR checklist -> https://git.redwood/replay-guard/runs/4321
